paragraphs: Qwen is an AI assistant for everyone, powered by the Qwen series models, according to Alibaba Cloud. It is free to use and open to all, and Alibaba Cloud says it is ready to help with creativity, collaboration, and endless possibilities. The Qwen family includes models for text, images, audio, and video, with multimodal understanding that processes and analyzes these types of information simultaneously. Alibaba Cloud says Qwen excels in advanced reasoning and problem-solving, and that it leverages real-time internet data to deliver comprehensive, logical, and actionable solutions.

The family is organised into several lines. Flagship models include Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash, a next-generation native omnimodal model, and Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate, which rebuilds real-time simultaneous interpretation with an Interleave architecture. Qwen-Image-2.1 is an open-source image model with 7B parameters in its visual generation component, unifying text-to-image generation and image editing. Qwen-Drive-1.0 is a vision-language foundation model for autonomous driving built on the natively multimodal Qwen3.5-4B. Qwen VLo is a unified model that understands and creates visuals.

Alibaba Cloud offers Qwen through the Qwen API, which uses an API format compatible with the OpenAI API, and through apps for Web, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. Qwen Cloud and an API Platform are also listed. The Qwen site provides Qwen Code, Research, and an Ambassador programme, and the models are available on GitHub.

price_limits.summary: Across the 53 versions, input prices run from $0.03 to $4 per million tokens and output prices from $0.13 to $12. Qwen3.7 Flash is the cheapest, at $0.03 per million input tokens and $0.13 per million output tokens. Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B has the largest context window, 1,048,576 tokens.

family_reading.text: Qwen is a large family, with 53 versions in the catalog and a wide spread of tiers. Across the whole family, 36 of 53 versions support reasoning and 35 publish open weights, so both are common but not universal. Context windows run from 32768 to 1048576 tokens, and inputs can include audio, image, text and video, while output is text only. The newest versions show the range: cheap Flash and small open models at a few cents per million input tokens, and Max tiers at $2 to $4 input and $6 to $12 output. That suggests the family suits long-context work, multimodal input and reasoning tasks, with open weights available for self-hosting. Limits are the text-only output, the cost of the largest tiers, and the fact that not every version supports reasoning or open weights.
